html:
SMTO-TSK-0018 — SMTO didn't recognize that way of stopping

GUID: 1af6325f-20dc-433c-9e2c-1dc9a4d72560
Slug: stop-mode-invalid
Domain: TSK · Subsystem: tsk

What happened

  • A request to stop a task asked for a stopping method SMTO doesn't have, so the stop wasn't sent. The task may still be running.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the conversation and select Stop current task. The app's Stop button always sends a stopping method SMTO understands.
  2. If a script or other tool sent the stop, change it to ask for instant or graceful stopping, or to leave the method out. Those are the only stopping methods SMTO accepts; leaving it out uses the task's normal stop setting.

What success looks like

  • The task shows Stopping and then Stopped in the conversation.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Until the task shows Stopped, assume it is still running.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Stop request supplied a mode other than omitted, "instant" or "graceful", so it was rejected before any cancellation was requested.

What this means

  • The Stop endpoint receives a mode outside omitted/default, instant or graceful. Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.

Why this can happen

  • The Stop endpoint receives a mode outside omitted/default, instant or graceful.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the supplied mode with the current Stop control contract.

How to fix it

  • Call the stop endpoint with mode omitted (use the run's Stop policy), "instant" or "graceful"; any other value returns 422 before cancellation. Then read the run status to confirm the Stop was accepted.
  • Choose a Stop mode advertised by the current task controls.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Stop uses an advertised mode and its accepted result is inspected.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
